SMTO-HTTP-0020 — SMTO used another name instead of the connection's exact name

GUID: f94405b3-649c-4481-9cfe-8469b3d5dc94
Slug: http-profile-key-not-exact
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • SMTO looked up a saved web service connection by a nickname or a slightly different spelling. For safety, SMTO only uses a saved connection when asked for it by its exact name, so nothing was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store and find the connection you want SMTO to use. Note its exact name as shown in the list. SMTO only accepts the connection's exact name, not a nickname or a different spelling.
  2. In the conversation, type @ in the message box and pick the connection from the Parameter Store list, or type its exact name, and ask SMTO to use it. Picking it from the list inserts the exact name, so the lookup matches.

What success looks like

  • SMTO connects using the named connection and continues without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't rename or copy the connection just to match the nickname; using the exact name is enough.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Parameter Store lookup matched a record whose normalized key differs from the supplied key, so the HTTP profile was selected by alias or inexact name and was refused.

What this means

  • Parameter lookup resolved a record whose normalized key differs from the supplied normalized key, indicating an alias or inexact selection. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Parameter lookup resolved a record whose normalized key differs from the supplied normalized key, indicating an alias or inexact selection.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the listed canonical profile key with the submitted selector.

How to fix it

  • exact_record (skills/http/connections.py) and HttpRequestCapability._execute reject a record whose normalized_key differs from normalize_parameter_key(supplied key), i.e. the lookup resolved through an alias. Use the canonical profile_key returned by http.inspect_connections or shown in Parameter Store.
  • Use the exact configured Parameter Store key returned by the current profile listing.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The request names the intended record's exact canonical key.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
